newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund future rally hangs in balance ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: Bund future rally hangs in balance ahead of data.

text.p: Bund futures remained in positive territory most of the day on Monday but well within recent ranges as traders readied for key German econoimc indicators later in the week.
At 1547 GMT, the DTB March Bund contract was up nine basis points, about in the middle of the day's range between 101.32 and 101.74.

Analysts said that with the market having posted solid gains much of this month, only fresh evidence of slow German economic growth could keep the rally going, and push the contract toward the high of 102.07.

"If after this week, the market has not posted any gains, we could be looking at ranges for a while," said Catherine Lee, bond market analyst at R.H. Wrightson & Associates. "At current levels, the market is looking a little vulnerable."

She and other analysts said a rally in the contract of more than two full points since the start of January hinges on the upcoming Ifo business sentiment index due out at 0900 GMT on Tuesday, December M3 money supply data due out early this week as well as inflation data that are also expected this week.
Speculation the Bundesbank may yet cut its repo rate could be renewed and lift Bunds if the data show a weak economy.
Several speeches from Bundesbank officials did not shed much light on interest rates on Tuesday.
Hans-Juergen Krupp, a noted dove, repeated warnings that the economy is growing slowly while Franz-Cristoph Zeitler simply said private investment has not yet emerged as a motor of economic growth.
The German yield curve, which was little changed on the day, showed traders did not put much stock in the comments.
The spread between two- and 10-year Bund yields narrowed by one basis point to 246 basis points.
Bunds continued to perform well against U.S. notes with the Bund/T-note spread widening out to 92 basis points -- again testing post-unification highs.
Analysts said the spread faces resistance around 100 basis points and the underlying economic fundamentals do not justify a spread that wide.
Lee said that with the dollar climbing to more than 1.60 to the mark that the need for a rate cut is diminishing and the Bundesbank is likely to leave rates steady for the near-term at least.
"If the Bundesbank were to cut interest rates now, there is a danger that the market would take it badly," she said.
The 10-year cash Bund was hardly changed 101.79 compared with 101.78, yielding 5.76 percent.
